content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp spikes in the history.
- Model shows strong upward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- When true prices spike sharply (e.g., >40), model fails to adjust downward quickly, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices in the history, failing to anticipate mean reversion or correction phases.
- Forecast horizon 30d exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — model takes longer to correct than actual market behavior.
- Model overfits to recent high prices, ignoring longer-term volatility or structural shifts.
- When true prices show a sharp downward correction after a spike, model continues upward trend, missing the reversal.
